limits: Two exposed native task families; one repeat; no held-out acceptance.
Same schedule across clients but Codex needed explicit executable binding; no cross-client causal comparison.
Development fixture semantics preserve real blocked routes; no consumer task outcome or human usability proof.
Provider input/cache counters retained separately; unknown billed cost, time to first useful action, true repair attempts and total operator maintenance cost.
Raw native receipts retained locally; portable hashes support identity, not public replay of model behavior.
Parallel host/model load and cache state uncontrolled; durations descriptive only.
No independent multilingual review, broad safety certification, official benchmark or production ROI claim.
